Tree repair and traversal logic for block slots, shreds, and consumed frontier management.

# Purpose
`fd_forest.c` implements the runtime logic for a forest data structure that tracks block slots, parent and child links, and repair state for a shred-based block stream. It provides the public lifecycle API for the forest object: [`fd_forest_new`](<#fd_forest_new>), [`fd_forest_join`](<#fd_forest_join>), [`fd_forest_leave`](<#fd_forest_leave>), [`fd_forest_delete`](<#fd_forest_delete>), [`fd_forest_init`](<#fd_forest_init>), [`fd_forest_fini`](<#fd_forest_fini>), [`fd_forest_verify`](<#fd_forest_verify>), and [`fd_forest_publish`](<#fd_forest_publish>). The code allocates all forest substructures inside shared memory, stores workspace global addresses, sets the version sequence with `fd_fseq`, and uses a magic value and alignment checks to validate object state. It also manages the root slot and prunes old tree state when a new root is published.

The file also contains the main update and query logic for block repair. Functions such as [`fd_forest_blk_insert`](<#fd_forest_blk_insert>), [`fd_forest_data_shred_insert`](<#fd_forest_data_shred_insert>), [`fd_forest_fec_insert`](<#fd_forest_fec_insert>), [`fd_forest_code_shred_insert`](<#fd_forest_code_shred_insert>), and [`fd_forest_fec_clear`](<#fd_forest_fec_clear>) update block records as data and FEC shreds arrive. The code keeps several maps and lists in sync, including `ancestry`, `frontier`, `subtrees`, `orphaned`, and `consumed`, and it advances the consumed frontier when a slot becomes complete. Iterator functions [`fd_forest_iter_init`](<#fd_forest_iter_init>), [`fd_forest_iter_next`](<#fd_forest_iter_next>), and [`fd_forest_iter_done`](<#fd_forest_iter_done>) expose the next shred request for repair. The file also includes print helpers for debugging the forest state.
